svc.name: Single Variable Calculus
svc.why: Delta is a derivative, P&L is an integral, and every Greek starts with the question this subject answers: how fast does one thing change with another?

mvc.name: Multivariable Calculus
mvc.why: An option price depends on spot, volatility and time at once — the Greeks are partial derivatives, and risk surfaces live in many dimensions.

prob.name: Probability
prob.credit: Statistics 110: Probability (Prof. Joe Blitzstein, Harvard University); lesson structure follows the public lecture series
prob.why: Fair value is an expectation, risk is a distribution, and every pricing model is a probability statement about tomorrow.

ode.name: Differential Equations
ode.why: Rates mean-revert, positions decay, hedges rebalance — writing change over time as an equation is the step before stochastic calculus adds the noise.

ra.name: Real Analysis
ra.why: Limits, convergence and continuity are assumed everywhere in quant finance — this is where they stop being hand-waves and become theorems.

opt.name: Optimization
opt.credit: the Optimization Bootcamp lecture playlist (YouTube); lesson structure follows the public series
opt.why: Portfolio construction, best execution and model calibration are all the same move: define a cost, respect the constraints, find the minimum.

stat.name: Statistics
stat.why: Every signal is an estimate and every backtest is a hypothesis test — statistics is how you know whether the market is telling you something or nothing.

ca.name: Complex Analysis
ca.credit: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.04, Complex Variables with Applications (Spring 2018)
ca.why: Characteristic functions and Fourier transforms price options fast (FFT pricing) — and they live in the complex plane.

tsa.name: Time-Series Analysis
tsa.why: Returns arrive in order — stationarity, autocorrelation and volatility clustering are properties of time series, and trading models are built on them.

dsp.name: Discrete Stochastic Processes
dsp.why: Order arrivals are Poisson processes, regimes are Markov chains, and stopping rules are martingale questions — randomness one step at a time, before continuous time.

sc.name: Stochastic Calculus
sc.credit: the stochastic-calculus lectures of MIT OpenCourseWare 18.642, Topics in Mathematics with Applications in Finance (Fall 2024)
sc.why: Prices move continuously and randomly — Brownian motion, Itô's lemma and SDEs are the calculus that makes Black–Scholes a theorem instead of a guess.

mff.name: Maths for Finance
mff.credit: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.642, Topics in Mathematics with Applications in Finance (Fall 2024)
mff.why: The destination: every subject on the roadmap applied to real pricing, hedging, portfolio and risk problems, the way a desk actually uses them.
